workflow: A data-processing operation iterates over an object’s internal format or storage while invoking user-controlled conversion logic for an input value.
The callback re-enters the same object and rebuilds its internal representation, releasing the storage used by the outer iteration.
The outer operation continues using its previously obtained pointer without revalidating the representation or reacquiring storage.
A later iteration dereferences the stale pointer, causing a use-after-free and process-terminating memory-safety failure instead of a recoverable mutation error.
summary: Reentrant mutation invalidates storage during iteration
decision_reason: The failure workflow materially matches re-entrant mutation invalidating storage while an outer clearing or processing operation still uses the original address, followed by a use-after-free.
